title: One, holy, catholic, apostolic (CCC 811)
hook: the four marks in the Creed

segments.voice: Yesterday, the body of Christ: many members, one body, with Christ as head. Your line was many members, one body. Whose joy or sorrow did you share? Today, four words that describe that body, said every Sunday. Day three hundred nineteen.

Every Sunday, in churches from Manila to Lagos to Chicago, a whole congregation stands and says the Creed. Near the end comes a line that's easy to rush: I believe in one, holy, catholic and apostolic Church. Four adjectives, said in about three seconds. The words go back to a council in Constantinople in the year 381, and many Christians outside the Catholic Church say them too, each understanding them in their own way. For Catholics they are called the four marks: the signs by which the Church is recognized. Today, slowly, one word at a time.
screen: `MANILA, LAGOS, CHICAGO.` → `FOUR WORDS IN THREE SECONDS.` → `CONSTANTINOPLE, 381.`

segments.voice: First, one. Paul writes, in the Douay-Rheims: "One Lord, one faith, one baptism." The Catechism says the Church is one because its source is one God, its founder is one Christ, and its soul is one Spirit. One doesn't mean identical. It means one faith, one set of sacraments, one line of shepherds, holding many languages and cultures together. Second, holy. People sometimes laugh at this one, and the Church admits why. It's full of sinners, and has been from the start. The Catechism says the Church is holy not because its members are, but because Christ made it his own and gives it the means of holiness. It also says, frankly, that the Church is at once holy and always in need of purification. Holy, and needing to be made clean, at the same time. Third, catholic. It's a Greek word, katholikos, from kath' holou: according to the whole. It means universal, and it also means whole: nothing missing. Around the year 107, Ignatius of Antioch, on his way to martyrdom in Rome, used the phrase catholic Church in a letter, one of the earliest written uses that survives. Fourth, apostolic. The Church is built on the apostles, keeps their teaching, and, Catholics say, is led by bishops who succeed them, in a line of laying on of hands going back to the beginning. So the four marks aren't four boasts. Catholics understand them as gifts from Christ and as tasks: to become more fully one, more holy, more truly whole, and more faithful to what the apostles handed on.
screen: `ONE LORD, ONE FAITH, ONE BAPTISM.` · `HOLY, AND NEEDING PURIFICATION.` · `KATH' HOLOU: ACCORDING TO THE WHOLE.` · `BUILT ON THE APOSTLES.` · then, large: `ONE, HOLY, CATHOLIC, APOSTOLIC.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: say the four words slowly. Settle, and breathe. On one breath out, say one. Let it sit. Think of all the people saying it with you around the world. Then holy, and think of one person whose goodness you've seen up close. Then catholic, and picture the whole, every language, every century. Then apostolic, and think of the people who handed faith down to you, or to someone you love. Four breaths, four words. Repeat them until the bell. The bell holds the time.
Marks of the Church. One, holy, catholic and apostolic: the four signs in the Creed by which Catholics say the Church is recognized. Today's word.
Your line: four marks. Today, pick one of the four and notice it somewhere: a sign of unity, of holiness, of the whole, or of something handed down. Day three hundred nineteen.

howItsDone: Catholics profess the four marks every Sunday and on solemnities in the Niceno-Constantinopolitan Creed, which is also said, with differences of understanding, by Orthodox and many Protestant churches.

fork.setup: someone points out that the Church is full of sinners and asks how Catholics can call it holy. what does the Catechism say?
options: that Christ makes it holy, and it always needs purification.
fork.reveal: holy because of Christ and the means of holiness he gives, and at the same time always in need of being made clean.

original.note: Greek: universal, whole, from kath' holou, according to the whole.

trapdoor: what you thought: catholic is just the name of a denomination.
what it means: one of four marks in the Creed, universal and whole, alongside one, holy and apostolic.
what a scholar hears: Constantinople 381; kath' holou; Ignatius of Antioch, Smyrnaeans 8, around 107; Lumen Gentium 8 on holy and always to be purified.
